text.p: Iraq's President Saddam Hussein removed Culture and Information Minister Abd-al-Ghani Abd-al-Ghafur from his post in a surprise reshuffle that is unlikely to herald major policy changes.
The other key ministers of foreign affairs, defence, interior remained unchanged in the two decrees signed by Saddam on Wednesday.
Abd-al-Ghafur was replaced by presidential adviser Hamed Youssef Hummadi, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) said on Thursday.

"Culture and Information Minister Abd-al-Ghani Abd-al-Ghafur is relieved from his post," said INA, quoting one of two presidential decrees. "Hamed Youssef Hummadi is appointed Minister of Culture and Information," said the other decree.
Abd-al-Ghafur, a senior member of the ruling Baath Party's Regional Command and Head of the Students and Youth Office of the party, had been appointed to the post in January 1996.
Hummadi had been the information minister before Abd-al-Ghafur.
Earlier this year Hummadi was elected to Iraq's National Assembly (parliament). He also heads the Culture and Information Committee in the Assembly.

During Baghdad's standoff with Washington in September over Iraq's military intervention in the Kurdish north, Saddam sent Hummadi to Turkey to argue against Ankara's plans to set up a security cordon in northern Iraq.
Turkey has said it wants to set up such a zone to prevent infiltration of Turkish Kurdish rebels fighting for self-rule in southeast Turkey but Iraq strongly opposes Ankara's plan.
